thread:
nora: Hey all, surgeon scheduled my knee arthroscopy for next month. Hospital finance sent a self-pay estimate and said they can't find my insurer in their system. I have the digital ID but no physical card. They want a deposit. Should I pay or wait?

aditya (People Ops): Sorry that's stressful, @nora. Two things to try before paying: 1) ask the facility for a predetermination of benefits (not just an estimate) and their billing NPI/tax ID; 2) ask the scheduler to submit a prior-authorization check with the insurer now. Both can prevent surprise out-of-network billing.

surgery-coord (Clinic): We can hold the deposit for 72h while the insurer is contacted. If member provides digital ID PDF + member/group, we re-run eligibility. Sometimes systems show the facility as out-of-network even when the contracted facility name differs.

nora: They said the system returned "no active coverage on file" so they want $1,200 deposit. I emailed a screenshot of the digital ID but they said screenshots aren't accepted.

aditya (People Ops): Provide the insurer PDF (portal > Documents > ID card > Download PDF). If they still won't accept it, ask for a written estimate showing CPTs, facility fees, surgeon fee line items, and the clinic's billing contact. We'll help chase the insurer.

claims-broker: If you pay, get a detailed receipt listing service codes (CPT/HCPCS), facility tax ID, and an itemized bill. You can submit that for reimbursement or ask insurer to reprocess if provider rebills. Also request a prior-authorization number in writing (if required for arthroscopy).

insurer-bot: Digital ID available: https://portal.insurer/ids/665554321.pdf :card_file_box: (expires 2027-10-01)

aditya (People Ops): Quick templates: 1) Prior auth eligibility check email for clinic to send to insurer; 2) Member claim/predetermination request if you pay out-of-pocket. Use the one below as a cover email for a predetermination request:

```
To: provider-services@insurer.example
Subject: Predetermination request  Member 665554321  Arthroscopy 2026-09-15
Body: Please adjudicate expected benefits for planned arthroscopy on 2026-09-15 for Member Nora L (Member ID 665554321, Group RW-00011). Attachments: signed surgery consent.pdf, expected procedure codes (CPT 29877), facility estimate.pdf.
Please confirm: (a) coverage and in-network status for facility and surgeon, (b) any required prior auth number, (c) estimated member financial responsibility (copay/deductible coinsurance).
```

nora: If I pay now and later insurer reprocesses as in-network, will I get refunded? How long does that take?

claims-broker: Yes, if insurer determines the provider/facility is in-network or approves the predetermination, they'll reprocess and refund according to plan terms. Timeline: predetermination/authorization ack usually 5-10 business days; EOB/reprocessing 2-6 weeks. Keep all receipts and the facility estimate.

aditya (People Ops): Also ask the facility to send a facility contract verification or name of the contracting entity. Sometimes the facility is contracted under a parent company name. That helps the insurer match network records.

surgery-coord (Clinic): We can request a contract name from our billing team but that can take 48-72h. If you want, we can pause the deposit while we do that.

nora: Thanks 1 appreciate the pause. One more: how do I get a paper card quickly? My surgeon insists on seeing a physical card at check-in.

insurer-bot: Request paper ID via member portal > Account Settings > Request ID Card. Expedited mailing available in some regions; phone requests may expedite by 3-5 business days.

aditya (People Ops): If the clinic needs proof now, send them the insurer PDF and a short cover note from us. If they still demand paper, we can ask our broker to request an expedited card. Reply here and I'll initiate.

nora: Please initiate expedited mailer, thanks. Also cc'd benefits@redwood.com on the estimate email.

aditya (People Ops): Done  broker notified. Final checklist for @nora: (1) get the predetermination or prior-auth in writing, (2) secure an itemized facility estimate with CPTs and tax ID, (3) if you pay, obtain an itemized receipt and save phone call notes, (4) cc benefits@redwood.com so we can escalate.

claims-broker: If insurer denies later, we can file an appeal and a provider-directory dispute if records show the facility should be in-network. Keep all documentation.

nora: Sending the PDF & consent now. Really appreciate the support :heart:
